ui_bugs.issue: ReferenceError: Cannot access 'openBriefById' before initialization. The iter66 hash-handler useEffect (lines 136-146) is declared BEFORE the useCallback that defines openBriefById (line 148). Since the useEffect dependency array `[cid, openBriefById]` and the body both read openBriefById synchronously, React throws a TDZ error on every render of Prepare — not just when the hash is present. This crashes the entire /app/prepare route.

action_items: FIX (CRITICAL): Move the `const openBriefById = useCallback(async (idOrItem) => {...}, [cid]);` block (currently at Prepare.jsx line 148) ABOVE the iter66 hash-handler useEffect (currently at line 136). This resolves the TDZ ReferenceError and unblocks both the hash deep-link AND the rest of the Prepare route. Recommended order: declare openBriefById first → then the hash useEffect. After the fix, retest /app/prepare#brief-{id} for: (a) auto-switch to Brief tab, (b) modal opens, (c) hash stripped via replaceState, (d) silent no-op when briefId doesn't exist.
critical_code_review_comments: Prepare.jsx 136-155: Classic JS hoisting trap with const + useCallback. const declarations are hoisted but in TDZ until the line is evaluated; the useEffect at line 136 captures `openBriefById` via its dep array which is evaluated when the function component body runs, BEFORE line 148 is reached. Result: every render of Prepare throws. Move the useCallback above the useEffect (or convert openBriefById to a regular async function declared before the effect — both fix TDZ).

ActiveWorkflowsRail tile clickability uses `onClick + window.location.assign` instead of a proper <Link to=...> from react-router-dom. Functionally works but bypasses SPA routing (causes a full page reload, loses scroll/state, defeats router prefetch). Consider switching to `<Link to={`/app/plays/${p.id}`}>` for consistency with the rest of the surface.

rca of the issue: Prepare.jsx hash handler crash · ROOT CAUSE: ReferenceError 'Cannot access openBriefById before initialization' caused by a JavaScript Temporal Dead Zone violation. const + useCallback declarations are hoisted but inaccessible until the line where they're assigned. The iter66 useEffect at line 136 lists `openBriefById` in its dependency array (line 146) and calls it in the body (line 143); both run during the function component's render pass, but `openBriefById` isn't assigned until line 148. RESULT: render throws on every mount of /app/prepare, blowing up the entire Catch-up route — not only the hash flow. REPRO: Visit /app/prepare while logged in (with or without #brief- hash). REPLAYS: 100% deterministic. MITIGATION: Move lines 148-155 (the openBriefById useCallback block) ABOVE the iter66 useEffect block (currently lines 133-146). One-line reordering. After the fix, the page renders, the hash handler fires when present, the modal opens, and the hash is stripped via history.replaceState.
